LTKA: The bani 'Anand' of Guru Amardas Ji, in Rag Ramkali.
Raamkalee, Third Mehl, Anand ~ The Song Of Bliss:
GE9G: Akal Purakh is One, and He is met through the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God. By True Guru's grace, He is obtained.
2UEB: Anandu = complete blossoming. Paia = has obtained.
O brother, O mother! (Within me) a complete blossoming has arisen, (because) I have come to meet the Guru.
I am in ecstasy, O my mother, for I have found my True Guru.
Joy has welled up, O my mother, for I have obtained my True Guru.
(Mae) O sant jano! Bliss arose in my buddhi from that very day on which I obtained the Satiguru.
BJ01: Sahj = the state of poise. Sahj seti = together with the state of poise. Mani = in the mind. Vadhai = ascendancy, a song that generates uplift.
I have met the Guru, and with that the state of poise has also been obtained (that is, by meeting the Guru my mind has ceased to waver); in my mind (as it were) the instruments of joy have struck up,
I have found the True Guru, with intuitive ease, and my mind vibrates with the music of bliss.
The True Guru, I have found with ease and within my mind resounds the music of bliss.
When I obtained the Satiguru, then (sahj seti) I became joined with gian; from this alone have joys become manifest in my mind.
6GJM: Paria = the fairies of the rags, the raginis. Rag ratan = beautiful rags.
The beautiful rags, together with their families and their consorts, have come (into my mind, as it were) to sing the songs of the praise of Prabhu.
The jewelled melodies and their related celestial harmonies have come to sing the Word of the Shabad.
The gem like measures and their families, have come to hymn the Guru's word.

The rags and raginis came in visible form; or, love and vairag; the family — truth, contentment, dharam, reflection, and again compassion, friendliness, gladness, and equanimity — the ranks made up of these virtues have (aia) been obtained through the uttering of (sabad) the Guru's updesh.
AR69: (You too) sing the song of the praise of Prabhu. Those who have settled the shabad of praise within the mind (within them a complete blossoming arises).
The Lord dwells within the minds of those who sing the Shabad.
They, who enshrine the Lord in their mind, sing the Gurbani of the Lord.
Therefore, O brother! Those who have settled Hari within the mind — through them, you too utter the Guru's updesh.
439Z: Nanak says, (within me too) bliss has come about, (because) I have met the Satiguru. ||1||
Says Nanak, I am in ecstasy, for I have found my True Guru. ||1||
Says Nanak, joy has ensued and I have attained to the True Guru.
Sri Guru Ji says: bliss has come to me from that very day on which I obtained the Satiguru. ||1||
Z58C: O my mind! Remain always (joined) with Prabhu.
O my mind, remain always with the Lord.
O my soul, ever abide you with your Lord.
O my mind! Remain always with Hari.
5AA1: Mann mere = O my mind! Sabhi = all. Visarana = that which removes.
O my mind! Always keep Prabhu in remembrance. That Prabhu is the remover of all sorrows.
Remain always with the Lord, O my mind, and all sufferings will be forgotten.
Ever abide you with your God, O my soul and He shall make you forget all sufferings.
O my mind! Remain in the company of Hari; from this the warding off of all sorrows will come about — the sense being, all sorrows will be removed.
YGK6: He is always your helper; He is capable of bringing all your works to completion.
He will accept You as His own, and all your affairs will be perfectly arranged.
He Shall own you and shall arrange all yours affairs.
That Hari will take your (angikaru) side, and from this He will set right all your work.
350Z: Samrathu = capable. Manahu = from the mind. Visare = you forget.
Why do you forget from (your) mind that Master who is capable of doing all things?
Our Lord and Master is all-powerful to do all things, so why forget Him from your mind?
The Lord is Omnipotent to do all things. Why Forget Him from your mind?
He who is the Master capable in all matters — why do you forget Him from the mind?
CF7N: Nanak says, O my mind! Remain always joined to the feet of Prabhu. ||2||
Says Nanak, O my mind, remain always with the Lord. ||2||
Says Nanak, O my soul, abide you with your God.
Sri Guru Ji says: O my mind! Remain always in the company of Hari, and make your supplication thus. ||2||
4GE3: O ever-abiding Master (-Prabhu)! (I beg the bliss of the mind at Your door, but) which thing is not in Your house?
O my True Lord and Master, what is there which is not in Your celestial home?
O my True Lord, what is that which You has not in Your home?
O True Master! What is there that is not in Your house — the sense being, everything is there.
4N3D: Ta = then. Sabhu kichhu = every thing. Dehi = You give. Su = that man. Pave = pavai, he obtains, he acquires.
In Your house every single thing is present; that man alone obtains it to whom You Yourself give.
Everything is in Your home; they receive, to whom You give.
Within Your home is everything, but he alone receives it, whom You givest.
In Your house there is indeed (sabhu kichhu) every substance; but he to whom You give, he obtains.
XG9Y: Siphati salah = greatness. Mani = in the mind. Vasave = vasavai, he settles.
(Then that man) settles Your Nam and Your praise within (his own) mind (by the grace of which bliss arises within him).
Constantly singing Your Praises and Glories, Your Name is enshrined in the mind.
He, who enshrines Your Name in his mind ever hymns Yours praise and excellences, O Lord.
O One of praise! They always perform Your extolling; and again, Your Nam alone they settle in the mind.
EWZF: Jin kai mani = in whose mind. Vaje = they sound. Sabad = the sounds of instruments, the notes of the rags. Ghanere = countless.

Those men in whose mind (Your) Nam dwells — within them, as it were, the blended notes of countless instruments begin to sound (that is, there arises in their mind the joy and eagerness that arises on hearing the blended music of many instruments).
The divine melody of the Shabad vibrates for those, within whose minds the Naam abides.
Many strains of rejoicing play of him in whose mind the Lord's Name abides.
Those in whose mind Your Nam has come to dwell — for them many instruments in the form of praise have sounded.
KUUL: Nanak says, O ever-abiding Master! In Your house there is no lack of any thing (and I beg the gift of bliss at Your door). ||3||
Says Nanak, O my True Lord and Master, what is there which is not in Your home? ||3||
Says Nanak, O my True Lord, what is that, which is not in Your mansion?
Sri Guru Ji says: O True Master! What is not in Your house — that is, everything is there. ||3||
LRXJ: (By Prabhu's mercy His) ever-stable Nam has (become) the support of my life.
The True Name is my only support.
The True Name is my only support.
The True Nam alone is my support.
176Q: That ever-abiding Nam has become the support of my life, which (Hari-Nam) has removed all my greeds.
The True Name is my only support; it satisfies all hunger.
The True Name, which has satisfied all my hunger, is my only support.
Such a True Nam has become my support, which has driven away all hungers.
82EB: Kari = having produced. Mani = in the mind. Ichha = the desires of the mind. Sabhi = all.
That Hari-Nam which, producing peace and happiness (within me), has come to settle in my mind; which (Hari-Nam) has fulfilled all the desires of my mind.
It has brought peace and tranquility to my mind; it has fulfilled all my desires.
Abiding in my mind, the Name has blessed me with peace and pleasure and fulfilled all my desires.
Again: it has made peace in the mind, and the Parmatma whose form is happiness has come to dwell in my mind. ☬ Of what kind is that Parmatma who has fulfilled all desires?
XMGJ: I make (myself) a sacrifice to my Guru, because all these bounties are the Guru's alone.
I am forever a sacrifice to the Guru, who possesses such glorious greatness.
I am eve a sacrifice to my Guru, who possesses such like excellences.
For this very reason I have always made my own self a sacrifice over the Gurus, whose these greatnesses are.
P8TM: Nanak says, O sant jano! Listen (to the Guru's shabad); form love for the Guru's shabad.
Says Nanak, listen, O Saints; enshrine love for the Shabad.
Says Nanak, hearken you, O saints, profess you love for the Lord's Gurbani.
Sri Guru Ji says: Listen, O sants! You too hold love for the Guru's updesh.
Q3P4: (Only by the Satiguru's mercy has Prabhu's) ever-abiding Nam (become) the support of my life. ||4||
The True Name is my only support. ||4||
The True Name is my only support.
And as for me, the True Nam alone is my support. ||4||
QLZ5: Vaje = they sound, they have sounded. Panch sabad = the blended notes of five kinds of instruments. Titu = in that. Titu ghari = in that heart-house. Sabhagai = in the fortunate one.
In that fortunate (heart-) house the blended notes of five kinds of instruments begin to sound (as it were),
The Panch Shabad, the five primal sounds, vibrate in that blessed house.
The five forms of music ring in that very fortunate house.
In that fortunate house the instruments of the five shabads have sounded.
4UD1: Titu sabhagai ghari = in that fortunate (heart-) house. Kala = power. Jitu ghari = in which house. Dharia = You have placed.

In whichever (heart-) house (O Prabhu! You) have placed Your power, in that fortunate (heart-) house the blended notes of five kinds of instruments begin to sound (as it were) (that is, in that heart complete bliss comes about),
In that blessed house, the Shabad vibrates; He infuses His almighty power into it.
In that very fortunate house(heart) into which the Lord has infused His might resound the strains.
In whichever house Vahiguru has placed His power in a special measure, in that fortunate house — the body, or the satsang — the shabads have sounded.
HBAQ: Panch dut = the five enemies, kam and the rest. Kantaku = a thorn. Kantaku kalu = terrifying Kal, the fear of death.
(O Prabhu!) You bring his five enemies, kam and the rest, under control, and You remove the terrifying Kal (that is, the fear of death).
Through You, we subdue the five demons of desire, and slay Death, the torturer.
O Lord, You makest man control the five demons and slyest the agonising death
He has brought the five duts, kam and the rest, under control in reliance upon You; and again, Kal, which was the giver of pain — that those persons have killed.
7859: Dhuri = from the very beginning. Karmi = by mercy. Si = se, those men. Nami = in the Nam.
But only those men join themselves to the Hari-Nam in whose destiny You, by Your mercy, have from the very beginning placed (the writ of simran).
Those who have such pre-ordained destiny are attached to the Lord's Name.
They, whose destiny You have so pre-ordained, O Lord, are attached to Your Name.
Those who have (paia) obtained good karam from the very beginning — O Hari! Those persons have become joined to (tudhu) Your Nam.
4RHQ: Anahad = an-had, sounding without being struck, unbroken, continuous. ||5||
Nanak says, in that heart-house happiness arises; in that heart (as it were) unbroken instruments sound. ||5||
Says Nanak, they are at peace, and the unstruck sound current vibrates within their homes. ||5||
Says Nanak, they obtain peace and in their heart-home plays the celestial strain.
Sri Guru Ji says: in his antahkaran happiness has arisen, and in his (ghari) heart the shabad has sounded unbroken; songs concerning You are being sung. ||5||
0225: Sachi liv = true longing, the longing that abides for ever, love for the ever-stable Prabhu. Deh = body. Nimani = something without support, of light worth.
Without the longing of the feet of the ever-abiding Prabhu (without the bliss of it), this (human) body remains something without support.
Without the true love of devotion, the body is without honor.
Without the true love, unhonoured is this body.
Without true love the body (nimani) is devoid of honour.
F8JR: Kia kare = what does it do? Whatever it does, it does only worthless works.
This body, left without support in the absence of love for Prabhu's feet, whatever it does, does only worthless works.
The body is dishonored without devotional love; what can the poor wretches do?
Bereft of the Lord's love, unhonoured is the human body. What can this poor thing do?
The body is devoid of honour without love; then what can this poor thing do — the sense being, it is fruitless.
224E: Banwari = O Master of the garden that is the world!
O Master of the world! You alone show mercy! (so that this may join itself to the Guru's shabad and be reformed) No other is even capable of setting it on a fitting path.
No one except You is all-powerful; please bestow Your Mercy, O Lord of all nature.
Without You, none else is omnipotent, Show You mercy to me, O Lord of the Forest.
Apart from You there is none capable of making the body fruitful; therefore, O Parmeshvar, Keeper of the forest that is the world! Show mercy, by which it may become fruitful.
TJQN: Savaria = it can be set on a fitting path.
Apart from You there is no other place where this body might be set on a fitting path. (Only by Your mercy) can it be reformed by joining itself to the Guru's shabad.
There is no place of rest, other than the Name; attached to the Shabad, we are embellished with beauty.
This body has no other place of rest than the Name, Attaching to the Name, it is embellished.
For the making fruitful of this body there is indeed no other place. This the gurmukhs have set right only by joining themselves to the Guru's updesh.
JUXQ: Vechariā = dependent on another, something helpless, under the sway of Maya. ||6||
Nanak says, without the love of Prabhu's feet this body is dependent on another (that is, under the sway of Maya), and whatever it does, it does only useless work. ||6||
Says Nanak, without devotional love, what can the poor wretches do? ||6||
Says Nanak, what can the wretched body (Creature) do without the Lord's Love?
Sri Guru Ji says: without the one love, what can this poor inert body do? ||6||
ZDQR: To say it, anyone will say that bliss has come to him; but the understanding of (real) bliss is had only from the Guru.
Bliss, bliss - everyone talks of bliss; bliss is known only through the Guru.
All talk of bliss and bliss, but the Real bliss is known only through the Guru.

'Bliss is obtained by me' — everyone says this over and over; but the full bliss has been known from the Guru. The sense being, the bliss of the knowledge of one's own real nature is obtained from the perfect Guru.
SCHK: Piaria = O beloved brother! Kripa kare = when the Guru shows mercy.
O beloved brother! The understanding of (real) bliss is always had from the Guru alone. (That man forms an acquaintance with real bliss upon whom the Guru) shows mercy.
Eternal bliss in known only through the Guru, when the Beloved Lord grants His Grace.
When one knows eternal bliss from the Guru, then the Loved-Lord shows His mercy to him.
Imperishable bliss has been known from the Guru's updesh. ☬ Question: How is the Guru met? ☬ Answer: O beloved Sikh! When Vahiguru shows mercy.
R29X: Kilvikh = sins. Anjanu = collyrium. Saria = he applies (to the eyes).
The Guru, showing mercy, cuts away the sins (from within him), and applies the collyrium of the understanding of spiritual life (to his eyes of discernment).
Granting His Grace, He cuts away our sins; He blesses us with the healing ointment of spiritual wisdom.
In His mercy the Lord cuts away his sins and blesses him with the slave of Divine knowledge.
Showing mercy, whosoever's sins He has cut away, again to him He has (saria) applied the collyrium of gian.
CU3H: Andarahu = from within the mind. Sachai = the ever-abiding (Parmatma). Sabadu = speech. Sabadu savaria = made the speech fitting (that is, he does not utter harsh words, words of slander and the like).
Those men from whose mind the attachment to Maya comes to an end — Akal Purakh makes their very speech fitting and sweet.
Those who eradicate attachment from within themselves, are adorned with the Shabad, the Word of the True Lord.
They, who from their mind drive away worldly love; their speech the True Lord embellishes.
Those whose moh has broken from within — their (sabadu) utterance the True One has set right.
G2W5: Ehu anandu hai = real spiritual bliss is this (that a man's harsh and slandering disposition simply does not remain). ||7||
Nanak says, real bliss is just this, and this bliss can be understood only from the Guru. ||7||
Says Nanak, this alone is bliss - bliss which is known through the Guru. ||7||
Says Nanak, this alone is the bliss, that bliss which the mortal can obtain only from the Guru.
Sri Guru Ji says: this which is the bliss of one's own real nature — that bliss has been known from the Gurus. ||7||

ZVK9: Baba = O Hari! Dehi = You give (the gift of bliss).
O Prabhu! That man to whom You give (the gift of spiritual bliss) obtains it.
O Baba, he alone receives it, to whom You give it.
O Father, that man alone obtains bliss, whom You givest, O Lord.
O Parmeshvar! He to whom You give, that person obtains.
NVTD: Hori vechariā = the other poor beings. Kia karahi = what can they do? Nothing avails them against Maya.
That man alone enjoys (this gift) to whom You give; for the other poor beings nothing avails (against the flood of Maya).
He alone receives it, to whom You give it; what can the other poor wretched beings do?
That man alone attains to it, whom You blesses with it, What can other poor mortals do?
That servant obtains to whom You give; what can the other poor ones do?
TK51: Iki = some beings. Bharami = in the wandering (of Maya). Dahdisi = in the ten directions.
Some men, gone astray in the wandering (of Maya) from the true path, run about in the ten directions; others (the fortunate ones) You join to Your Nam and (their birth) You set right.
Some are deluded by doubt, wandering in the ten directions; some are adorned with attachment to the Naam.
Some stray in doubt and wander in ten directions. Some are bedecked by attachment to the Lord's Name.
Some, gone astray through delusion, wander in the ten directions. Some who have become joined to Your Nam — their birth You have set right.
BCFP: (In this way, by Your mercy,) those to whom Your will becomes dear — by the Guru's grace their mind becomes pure (and they enjoy spiritual bliss,
By Guru's Grace, the mind becomes immaculate and pure, for those who follow God's Will.
By Guru's grace, Immaculate becomes the mind of those, to whom the Lord's will is agreeable.
Those to whom, by the Gurus' mercy, Your will is pleasing — their mind has become pure.
DW95: (But) Nanak says, (O Prabhu!) he to whom You grant (the gift of spiritual bliss), he alone can enjoy it. ||8||
Says Nanak, he alone receives it, to whom You give it, O Beloved Lord. ||8||
Says Nanak, O Love; that person alone obtains bliss whom You give.
Sri Guru Ji says: he to whom You give the accepting of Your will, O Beloved! That person alone obtains You. ||8||
05E5: Akath = He whose virtues cannot all be told.
O beloved sant jano! Come, let us (together) speak the words of the praise of the Parmatma of boundless virtues,
Come, Beloved Saints, let us speak the Unspoken Speech of the Lord.
Come, O dear saints, let us utter the discourse of the ineffable Lord.
O beloved sants! Come, let us join together and make (ap) the discourse of the Guru.
FU61: Karah = let us do. Kitu duarai = by what means? Keri = of
Let us hear and tell the tales of that Prabhu whose virtues are beyond telling. (But if you should ask) by what means that Prabhu is met?
How can we speak the Unspoken Speech of the Lord? Through which door will we find Him?
Let us speak of the Ineffable Lord, By what means can we find Him?
Let us make the (kahani) discourse of Parmeshvar, and let us make this reflection: by what means, by what sadhan, is (akath) Hari obtained?
3GVV: Saupi = hand over. Hukami mannniai = if (Prabhu's) hukam is accepted (upon the head and brow).

(Then the answer is this, that instead of handing your own self over to Maya) hand over your body, mind, wealth, everything, to the Guru; (in this way) if the Guru's hukam becomes sweet to you, then Parmatma is met.
Surrender body, mind, wealth, and everything to the Guru; obey the Order of His Will, and you will find Him.
Surrender all your body, soul and wealth to the Guru and submit to his will, thus shall you obtain the Lord.
But having handed over body, mind and wealth, all, to the Gurus, and again upon the (manniai) accepting of the hukam of Parmeshvar, Parmeshvar is obtained.
2TCU: (So, sant jano!) Walk according to the Guru's hukam and sing always the bani of the praise of the ever-abiding Prabhu.
Obey the Hukam of the Guru's Command, and sing the True Word of His Bani.
Obey you the Guru's order and sing you the True Gurbani.
Therefore accept the hukam of the Guru, and sing the True Bani.
QDB5: Nanak says, O sant jano, listen! (The right path for meeting Him and for enjoying spiritual bliss is just this, that) you should keep telling the tales of that indescribable Prabhu. ||9||
Says Nanak, listen, O Saints, and speak the Unspoken Speech of the Lord. ||9||
Says Nanak, hearken O you saints, narrate you the inexpressible anecdote of the Lord.
Sri Guru Ji says: O sants! Listen, and utter the discourse of the Indescribable. ||9||
JN46: Kinai = by any man at all.
O restless mind! By cleverness no one at all has obtained (spiritual bliss).
O fickle mind, through cleverness, no one has found the Lord.
O my mercurial mind, no one has ever obtained the Lord through cleverness.
O restless mind! By cleverness no one has obtained Bhagvant.
3LD3: Mann meria = O my mind! {the tippi on the word 'mann' is only to add a matra; the actual word is simply 'man'}.
O my mind! Listen (attentively): no being at all has obtained (the bliss of union with Parmatma) by cleverness.
Through cleverness, no one has found Him; listen, O my mind.
By cleverness no one has obtained God, hearken you, O my soul!
O my mind! Listen: by cleverness no one has obtained it.
27NL: Jini = which (Maya). Etu bharami = in this delusion, that attachment is a sweet thing. Bhulaia = cast on the wrong road.

(That one should remain caught within in the beguiling Maya, and outwardly desire spiritual bliss by mere talk — this cannot be.) This Maya is very strong in catching beings in its attachment; it has cast them into this delusion, that attachment is a sweet thing, and in this way it keeps them on the wrong road.
This Maya is so fascinating; because of it, people wander in doubt.
Fascinating is this mammon, which has so much strayed the mortal in doubt.
This which is Maya, it is the beguiler, which has led the being astray into the delusion of this world.
S5RG: Tinai = that same (Prabhu). Jini = which (Prabhu). Thagauli = the thag-buti, the drug of the cheat.
(But what is even in the being's power?) That Prabhu who fastened upon the beings the thag-buti of attachment to Maya — He Himself has created this beguiling Maya.
This fascinating Maya was created by the One who has administered this potion.
This charming mammon too is the creation of Him, who has spread the illusion.
But that beguiling Maya was made by that Vahiguru who applied the deception of delusion.
DKG7: (So, O my mind! Instead of making yourself a sacrifice to Maya) make yourself a sacrifice to that Prabhu alone who has attached this sweet attachment (for only then does this sweet attachment come to an end).
I am a sacrifice to the One who has made emotional attachment sweet.
I make myself a sacrifice to Him, who has rendered to Him, who has rendered worldly love sweet to the mortals.
To that Vahiguru who has attached the sweet attachment, over Him I have made my own self a sacrifice.
UW8N: Nanak says, O my restless mind! By cleverness no one has found (the spiritual bliss of union with Parmatma). ||10||
Says Nanak, O fickle mind, no one has found Him through cleverness. ||10||
Says Nanak, O fickle man, none has ever obtained God by cleverness.
Sri Guru Ji says: O restless mind! By cleverness no one has obtained Vahiguru. ||10||
HLNA: O beloved mind! (If you long for lasting spiritual bliss then) always keep the True Prabhu safe (within yourself)!
O beloved mind, contemplate the True Lord forever.
O my loved soul, ever contemplate you the True one.
O beloved mind! Always cherish the True One.
DER9: This family that you see — it will not go through with you.
This family which you see shall not go along with you.
This family, which you see, shall not go with you.
O mind! This family that you see will not go with you.
F6T1: Why do you become caught in the attachment to this family? It cannot keep company with you to the very end.
They shall not go along with you, so why do you focus your attention on them?
It shall no depart with you, Why fix you your mind therewith?
That which is not going to go with you at all — why then do you attach your chit to it?
6ES4: Mule na = not at all. Kichai = ought to be done. Jitu = by which. Anti = at the end, in the end
That work by the doing of which one must wring one's hands in the end — that work should never be done at all.
Don't do anything that you will regret in the end.
Do you not ever such deed, of which you may have to repent in the end.
Such work should never be done, by which at the end we must feel remorse.
CS43: Listen (attentively) to the Satiguru's teaching; this teaching of the Guru ought always to be kept in mind.
Listen to the Teachings of the True Guru - these shall go along with you.
Hear you the True Guru's instruction, which shall go along with you.
O mind! Listen to the updesh of the Satigurus, which at the end will be your helper.
640W: Nanak says, O beloved mind! (If you long for bliss then) keep the ever-abiding Parmatma safe (within yourself) at every moment. ||11||
Says Nanak, O beloved mind, contemplate the True Lord forever. ||11||
Says Nanak, O my dear mortal ever meditate you on the True Lord.
Sri Guru Ji says: O beloved mind! Always cherish the True One, and make your praise thus. ||11||
0Q8G: Agam = O unreachable Prabhu! Agochara = O agochar Hari! Agochar = a-go-char, that which the organs of perception cannot reach.

(O beloved mind! Always keep Prabhu safe within yourself, and make your supplication before Him thus —) O unreachable Hari! O Prabhu who remains beyond the reach of the senses! No one has found the limit (of Your virtues).
O inaccessible and unfathomable Lord, Your limits cannot be found.
O my Inaccessible and Inapprehensible Lord, Yours limit can be known not.
O Parmeshvar! You who are hard to know by mind and speech, no one has found Your limit.
5D6H: Kinai = by anyone at all. Apu = one's own form. Janahe = janahi, You know.
You alone know Your own (real) form; no other being can find the end of Your virtues.
No one has found Your limits; only You Yourself know.
No one has found Your end, You alone knowest Yours ownself.
No one has found Your limit; You alone know Your own self.
1GVQ: Sabhi = all. Akhi = having spoken. Vakhanae = vakhanai, to describe. Ko = any being!
How could any other being tell of (Your virtues) by speaking? All these beings are but a play You Yourself have set going.
All living beings and creatures are Your play; how can anyone describe You?
Men and other creatures are all Your sport. BY what words can anyone describe and narrate You.
This which is the subtle and gross creation, it is all Your own play that has been made; what can anyone describe of Your accounts?
PWVW: Akhahi = You speak. Vekhahi = You watch over. Jini = by You who.
In every being it is You Yourself who speak, and every being You Yourself watch over — it is You who do this, who brought this world into being.
You speak, and You gaze upon all; You created the Universe.
It is You, who created the world and who speakest and seest all.
The one who speaks and the one who sees is all You alone, You who have brought forth this world.
MRE6: Nanak says, (O my beloved mind! Make your supplication to Prabhu thus —) You are for ever unreachable; (no being has ever) found the limit (of Your virtues). ||12||
Says Nanak, You are forever inaccessible; Your limits cannot be found. ||12||
Says Nanak, You, O Lord, are ever beyond reach. Yours end can be found not.
Sri Guru Ji says: You are for ever hard to attain; for this very reason no one at all has found Your limit. ||12||
P4XV: Suri = devtas. Muni jan = muni folk, rishis. Amritu = the Nam-water that gives spiritual bliss.
(Spiritual bliss is such an) amrit (that) the devtas, men and munis go about searching for it, (but) this amrit is had from the Guru alone.
The angelic beings and the silent sages search for the Ambrosial Nectar; this Amrit is obtained from the Guru.
The angelic persons and the silent sages search for the Divine Nectar, That Nectar I have obtained from the Guru.
The devtas and men and muni folk who search for that (amritu) bliss of the atma — that atmic bliss we have obtained from the Gurus.
01SM: Guri = the Guru. Mani = in the mind. Sabhi = all.
That man upon whom the Guru showed mercy obtained (this) amrit, (because) he settled the ever-abiding Prabhu within his own mind.
This Amrit is obtained, when the Guru grants His Grace; He enshrines the True Lord within the mind.
He, to whom the Guru shows mercy, obtains the Nectar and keeps the True Lord enshrined in his mind.
When the Gurus showed mercy, then the bliss of the atma was obtained; and again, true happiness was settled in the mind.
VZHF: Iki = many beings. Vekhi = having seen (the Guru). Parsani = to touch (the Guru's feet).
O Prabhu! All the beings and creatures You alone have created (You alone impel them; by Your impulse alone) many beings come, having had the darshan (of the Guru), to touch (his) feet,
All living beings and creatures were created by You; only some come to see the Guru, and seek His blessing.
All the sentient beings You has created, O Lord, but so rare ones who see the Guru and seek his protection.
The subtle and gross beings are all created by You alone. Some gurmukhs have indeed beheld Your form; and one seeker has only now come to touch the satsang.
PPYM: Bhala bhaia = seems sweet, seems dear.
the Satiguru seems dear to them (and by the Satiguru's grace their) greed, avarice and egotism are removed.
Their greed, avarice and egotism are dispelled, and the True Guru seems sweet.
His greed, avarice and egotism are dispelled and the True Guru seems sweet to him.
His greed, avarice and pride have been removed, so the Satigurus were pleased with him; or, he to whom the Satigur's updesh became dear.
V50J: Nanak says, that man with whom Prabhu is pleased has obtained the amrit (in the form of spiritual bliss) from the Guru. ||13||
Says Nanak, those with whom the Lord is pleased, obtain the Amrit, through the Guru. ||13||
Says Nanak, he with whom the Lord is pleased, obtains the Name nectar through the Guru.
Sri Guru Ji says: he upon whom He Himself has been merciful, he has obtained the bliss of the atma from the Gurus. ||13||
WR06: Bhagat = men who enjoy spiritual bliss. Chal = way of living.
(Those fortunate men who enjoy spiritual bliss are the bhagats, and those) bhagats' way of living is (always) apart (from the people of the world),
The lifestyle of the devotees is unique and distinct.
Peculiar is the way of life of the saints.
The way of the bhagats is apart from the world.
QPB1: Nirali = apart. Keri = of. Bikham = hard. Margi = upon the road.
(it is a settled thing that those) bhagats' way of living is apart (from others). They walk upon a (very) hard road.
The devotees' lifestyle is unique and distinct; they follow the most difficult path.
Peculiar is the way of life of the saints. They tread the difficult path.
The way of the bhagats is separate, because it is hard — for those bhagats have to walk on the hard road of bhagti.
F6SD: They renounce greed, avarice, egotism and the craving for Maya, and they do not speak much (that is, they do not go about proclaiming their own repute).
They renounce greed, avarice, egotism and desire; they do not talk too much.
They renounce avarice, covetousness, pride and talk not much.
Again: eating beyond what is needed for bare subsistence is lab; and lobh in the form of hoarding; and pride; and again, having renounced trishna, they also do not (bahutu) speak without restraint.
RE0D: Khanniahu = than the khanda, than the sword. Valahu = than a hair. Niki = fine. Etu margi = upon this road.

To walk upon this road (is a very hard game, because this road) is sharper than the edge of the khanda and finer than a hair (the possibility of falling from it remains at every moment, because worldly craving pushes the mind's poise off balance).
The path they take is sharper than a two-edged sword, and finer than a hair.
They go by this road which is sharper than the two-edged sword and finer than a hair.
Its edge is sharper than the khanda, and again finer than a hair. Upon this road, which is the understanding of bhagti, those bhagats have to (jana) walk.

6UV1: But those who by the Guru's grace have cast off self-regard — their (worldly) craving comes to an end in the remembrance of Hari-Prabhu.
By Guru's Grace, they shed their selfishness and conceit; their hopes are merged in the Lord.
They, who shed their self-conceit by Guru's grace, their aspiration merges in the Lord.
Those who by the Gurus' mercy have renounced self-regard, and whose craving is absorbed in the bhagti of Hari — the sense being, those who have no craving for other things.
34U3: Jugahu jugu = in every age, always, at all times ||14||
Nanak says, the way of living of the bhagats (who enjoy spiritual bliss) has come down apart (from the world) from all time. ||14||
Says Nanak, the lifestyle of the devotees, in each and every age, is unique and distinct. ||14||
Says Nanak, wondrous is the way of the Lord's slaves in every age.
Sri Guru Ji says: the (chal) practice of the bhagats is (jugahu jugu) in all the ages — the sense being, always and always — apart. ||14||
4SA2: Chalah = we beings walk. Horu = further secret. Kia jana = I do not know.
O Master-Prabhu! As You set (us beings) walking (upon the road of life), so we walk (that is all — only this much understanding has come to me); I do not know any further secret of Your virtues.
As You make me walk, so do I walk, O my Lord and Master; what else do I know of Your Glorious Virtues?
As You makest me walk, so do I walk, O Lord, what more can I know of Yours merits?
O Master! As You cause us to walk, in that same way we walk; what else do I know, as to which virtues are in You?
K5MB: Margi = upon the road (of bliss). Pavahe = pavahi, You place.
(This alone I have understood, that) by whatever road You set us walking, by that road we walk. Those men whom You set upon the road (of enjoying spiritual bliss),
As You cause them to walk, they walk - You have placed them on the Path.
They whom You puttest on Your path; as You makest them walk, so do they walk.
In whatever manner You cause them to walk, in that same manner these beings walk. And again, those persons whom You place upon the road of bhagti, they alone fall into it.
92ET: Laihi = You attach. Si = those men. Dhiave = dhiavahi, they meditate.
those whom You show mercy and join to Your own Nam, those men remember the Hari-Nam for ever.
In Your Mercy, You attach them to the Naam; they meditate forever on the Lord, Har, Har.
They whom You, in Your mercy, appliest to Your Name, ever reflect on You, O my Lord-Gold.
Showing mercy, those whom You attach to the Nam — those persons, O (Hari) Vahiguru! meditate upon Your Nam.
7ZH9: Whichever man You cause to hear Your own bani of praise (whom You impel toward hearing it), those men, (having reached) the Guru's door, enjoy spiritual bliss.
Those whom You cause to listen to Your sermon, find peace in the Gurdwara, the Guru's Gate.
He, whom You makest hear Yours discourse gathers peace from the Guru's door.
And again, he to whom You recite Your own discourse, those persons obtain happiness by hearing it through the Gurus.
SKVC: Tivai = in that same way, just so ||15||
Nanak says, O ever-abiding Master! As it pleases You, so You set (us beings) walking upon the road of life. ||15||
Says Nanak, O my True Lord and Master, you make us walk according to Your Will. ||15||
Says Nanak, O my True Lord, You makest men walk, as You pleasest.
Sri Guru Ji says: O True Master! In whatever way it pleases You, in that same way You cause the beings to walk. ||15||
Q51G: Sohila = a song of joy, a song that gives bliss.
This beautiful shabad (of the Satiguru) is the song that gives (spiritual) bliss,
This song of praise is the Shabad, the most beautiful Word of God.
This beauteous Gurbani is all praise of the Lord.
This (sabadu), the praise in the form of the Guru's updesh, is very beautiful.
PXYG: (know it for certain that) the beautiful shabad which the Satiguru has recited is for ever the giver of spiritual bliss.
This beauteous Shabad is the everlasting song of praise, spoken by the True Guru.
This beauteous Gurbani, uttered by the True Guru is the Eternal Lord's praise.
The praise in the form of the Guru's updesh is for ever (suhava) beautiful; but he to whom the Satigurus have recited the updesh, he has heard it.
9F6P: Ehu = this sohila. Manni = in the mind {the tippi on the letter 'm' is only to add a matra; the actual word is simply 'man'}.
But this Guru-shabad dwells in the mind of those upon whose forehead the writ inscribed from the very beginning comes to light.
This is enshrined in the minds of those who are so pre-destined by the Lord.
This Gurbani is enshrined in the minds of those, why are so destined by the Primal Being.
This has come to dwell in the mind of those for whom it came written in the records from the very beginning.
1CEH: Iki = many beings. Gali = by mere talking.
Very many such men go about (in whose mind the Guru-shabad has not come to dwell, but who) talk (about spiritual knowledge). By mere talk spiritual bliss has come to no one.
Some wander around, babbling on and on, but none obtain Him by babbling.
Some go about walking much but no one obtains the Lord by babbling.
Some go about talking a great deal, but by talking no one has obtained it.
S5T5: Nanak says, the shabad recited by the Satiguru is itself the giver of spiritual bliss. ||16||
Says Nanak, the Shabad, this song of praise, has been spoken by the True Guru. ||16||
Says Nanak, the True Guru has revealed the beauteous Gurbani to the world.
Sri Guru Ji says: this praise which is in the form of the Guru's updesh — He has recited it only to the one upon whom the Gurus have been merciful. ||16||
EF6Z: (By virtue of the Guru's shabad) those men who remembered the Nam of Parmatma (within them such bliss arose that the relishes of Maya no longer drew them, and) those men became men of pure living.
Those humble beings who meditate on the Lord become pure.
Pure become the persons, who meditate on the Lord.
Those servants have become pure who have meditated upon Hari.
T3V9: Gurmukhi = having taken the Guru's shelter.
Whoever took the Guru's shelter and remembered the Nam of Hari became of pure conduct.
Meditating on the Lord, they become pure; as Gurmukh, they meditate on Him.
They who by Guru's grace contemplate God, contemplate God, are rendered immaculate.
Those who have meditated upon Hari have become pure; but those who have meditated by way of the Gurus, their meditation is fruitful.
5FF5: Sahit siu = together with. Kutanb = family. Sabaia = all of it.
(By contact with them) their mother, father and the members of their family became of pure living; whoever kept their company, all of them became pure.
They are pure, along with their mothers, fathers, family and friends; all their companions are pure as well.
They are pure with their mother, father, family and good friends and all their associates are pure as well.
Together with mother and father, and again with the family, they have become pure; and their sangat too is all pure.
Z3MV: The Hari-Nam (is such a spring of bliss that) those who recite it become pure and those who hear it become pure; those who settle it within the mind, they too become pure.
Pure are those who speak, and pure are those who listen; those who enshrine it within their minds are pure.
They who utter God's Name are holy, they who hear it are holy and holy are they who treasure it in their mind.
Those who speak it are pure, and those who hear it are pure. And again, those too are pure who have settled it in the mind.
YRCK: Nanak says, those men who took the Guru's shelter and remembered the Hari-Nam have become of pure conduct. ||17||
Says Nanak, pure and holy are those who, as Gurmukh, meditate on the Lord, Har, Har. ||17||
Says Nanak, pious are they, who under the Guru's instruction, ponder over the Lord-Master.
Sri Guru Ji says: those persons are pure who have meditated upon the Hari Hari Nam by way of the Gurus. ||17||
C5TC: Karmi = by (outwardly religious) works, by way of karam-kand. Sahju = poise, spiritual bliss.

While one remains caught in the attachment to Maya, anxiety and dread stay in the mind for ever; (this) anxiety and dread is not removed without spiritual bliss, (and) spiritual bliss cannot be produced by performing works that only look religious from the outside.
By religious rituals, intuitive poise is not found; without intuitive poise, skepticism does not depart.
By rituals, Divine knowledge is produced not and without Divine knowledge doubt does not depart.
To the mere performers of karam-kand, (sahju) gian is not produced. Without the knowledge of one's own real nature the doubt of the mind does not depart.
Z31K: Sahsa = the anxiety and dread (arising from attachment to Maya). Kitai sanjami = by any method. Rahe = grew weary.
Very many men have worn themselves out performing (such) works, but the mind's anxiety and dread does not go by any such method.
Skepticism does not depart by contrived actions; everybody is tired of performing these rituals.
Doubt departs not by any contrivance. People have grown weary of performing ceremonial rites.
By any other means doubt does not depart; very many have gone on performing works. ☬ Question:
ADUT: Malinu = soiled. Kitu = by what? Kitu sanjami = by what method?
(For as long as) the mind is in dread (for that long) it stays soiled; this soil of the mind is not washed off by any (outward) device.
The soul is polluted by skepticism; how can it be cleansed?
Through doubt the soul is rendered filthy. By what means can it be cleansed?
Through doubt the (jiu) mind has become soiled; by what means may it be washed — the sense being, how may the being become pure? ☬ Answer:
SB6Z: Join yourself to the Guru's shabad, keep your chit joined for ever to the feet of Parmatma; (if) the mind (is to be washed, then wash it) thus.
Wash your mind by attaching it to the Shabad, and keep your consciousness focused on the Lord.
Attaching yourself to the Name, wash you your soul and continue to fix your mid on God.
O brother! Joining yourself to the Guru's updesh, wash the mind; and again, remain with your chit attached to the Hari-Nam.
FYD3: Nanak says, it is by the Guru's grace alone that spiritual bliss arises (within a man), and in this way the mind's anxiety and dread is removed. ||18||
Says Nanak, by Guru's Grace, intuitive poise is produced, and this skepticism is dispelled. ||18||
Says Nanak, by Guru's grace, Divine knowledge wells up and thus is this doubt dispelled.
Sri Guru Ji says: by the mercy of the Gurus gian is produced; this doubt which there is, it departs in this manner. ||18||
HSD3: Jiahu = from the soul, from within the mind.
(Men who perform only outwardly religious works) stay soiled in the mind (with vices) and seem pure only to the eye.
Those who are (maile) false in the soul, and again appear (nirmal) clean from the outside.
SHSP: And those men who appear pure from the outside but are inwardly given to vice — understand that they have wasted their life as a gambler loses his wealth at dice.
Those who are outwardly pure and yet polluted within, lose their lives in the gamble.
They, who are pure without and filthy within, lose their life in gamble.
Clean from the outside and (jiahu), that is inwardly, (maile) deceitful — those have lost their birth in the gamble of the world.
5BTD: (Inwardly) the heavy disease of craving for Maya keeps eating them; (in the greed of Maya) they have kept death forgotten.
They contract this terrible disease of desire, and in their minds, they forget about dying.
They contract this dire disease of greed and in their mind, forget death.
This great disease in the form of trishna has fastened upon them; through this alone they have let the thought of dying slip from the mind.
ELA8: Betale = ghosts, those out of step, gone astray.

(To appear religious in people's eyes they cite the Vedas and other religious books in praise of their outwardly religious works, but) the excellent teaching of remembering Prabhu's Nam that is in the Vedas and other religious books — to that they pay no attention, and they move about in the world like ghosts (they stay out of step with the rhythm of life).
In the Vedas, the ultimate objective is the Naam, the Name of the Lord; but they do not hear this, and they wander around like demons.
The Name is the best thing in the Vedas. That they hear not and wander like demons.
In the Vedas that which is the excellent Nam, that indeed they do not hear; and they wander about in the manner of ghosts — the sense being, they are impure.
4U4N: Nanak says, those who have abandoned the Nam of Parmatma and who are caught in the attachment to Maya — understand that they have lost the game of their life at dice. ||19||
Says Nanak, those who forsake Truth and cling to falsehood, lose their lives in the gamble. ||19||
Says Nanak, they, who forsake truth and cling to falsehood, lose their life in gamble.
Sri Guru Ji says: those who have renounced the True One and are attached to falsehood, those persons have lost their birth in the gamble. ||19||
5HQX: Those men are pure in mind and pure outwardly as well,
Those who are pure in the soul and again pure from the outside as well.
V34W: Satigur te = had from the Guru, that whose updesh has come from the Guru. Karni = conduct, the work fit to be done. Kamani = has earned.

who perform that earning (of the building of conduct) whose instruction is had from the Guru — they are pure in mind and pure outwardly as well (that is, their dealings with the world too are fitting); they remain pure outwardly and clean within.
Those who are outwardly pure and also pure within, through the Guru, perform good deeds.
They, who are pure without and pure within, do good deeds through the True Guru.
Clean from the outside as well, and (jiahu) clean from within as well; and having taken the updesh from the Satigurus, they have earned good conduct.
ALMK: Kur = attachment to Maya. Soi = news. Mansa = the stirring of the mind, the stirring of attachment to Maya in the mind. Sachi = in the simran of Prabhu.
The Maya-born stirring of their mind comes to an end in simran itself; (so much spiritual bliss arises within them that) news of the attachment to Maya does not even reach their mind.
Not even an iota of falsehood touches them; their hopes are absorbed in the Truth.
Even the very intelligence of falsehood reaches them not and their desire is merged in truth.
To them the (soi) news of falsehood does not even reach, because their mansa is absorbed in the True One.
XY83: Vanjare = men come (into the world) to trade (in bhagti).

(Beings have come into the world to trade in the merchandise of spiritual bliss) — those trader-beings alone are called good who (by walking the road the Guru showed and by earning the Nam) have made the precious human birth fruitful.
Those who earn the jewel of this human life, are the most excellent of merchants.
They, who earn the jewel of human birth, are the most excellent merchants.
Those who have earned — that is, made fruitful — the priceless human birth, those (vanjare) beings are good.
MAS1: Nanak says, those men whose mind becomes pure (within whom spiritual bliss comes about) remain for ever (in their innermost self) at the feet of the Guru. ||20||
Says Nanak, those whose minds are pure, abide with the Guru forever. ||20||
Says Nanak, they whose mind is pure abide ever with the Lord.
Sri Guru Ji says: those whose mind is pure, they remain for ever with the Guru's updesh. ||20||
E30Z: Seti = with. Sanmukhu = able to hold his face before, of unshamed face. Hovai = wishes to be.
If any Sikh wishes to be able to hold up his face before the Guru,
If a Sikh turns to the Guru with sincere faith, as sunmukh
If any disciple becomes truly faithful to the Guru;
If any Sikh of the Gurus should become sanmukh with the Gurus,
6VWC: Jiahu = from the heart. Gur nale = at the Guru's feet.

that Sikh who wishes that he should not have to lower his eyes before the Guru on account of some hidden fault — (then there is only one road, that) he should abide with a true heart at the Guru's feet.
if a Sikh turns to the Guru with sincere faith, as sunmukh, his soul abides with the Guru.
If any sikh turns towards his Guru, his soul abides with the Guru.
If any Sikh should become sanmukh, and should remain with the Guru from the soul.
HBZ7: Samale = keep in remembrance, keep settled.
Let the Sikh give the Guru's feet a place within his own heart, and keep them safe within his own soul.
Within his heart, he meditates on the lotus feet of the Guru; deep within his soul, he contemplates Him.
He heartily meditate on the Guru's feet and remembers him in his mind.
And again, having meditated in the heart upon the feet of the Gurus, let him within contemplate his own real form.
YF6T: Casting off self-regard, let him remain for ever under the Guru's protection, and know none other than the Guru (as the means of his spiritual life and bliss).
Renouncing selfishness and conceit, he remains always on the side of the Guru; he does not know anyone except the Guru.
Renouncing his self-conceit, he remains ever on the side of the Guru. Without the Guru, he knows not any other.
Having renounced self-regard, let him remain for ever under the protection of the Gurus, and let him know none other than the Guru as protector.

2UCM: Nanak says, O sant jano! Listen — that Sikh (alone) can remain with a radiant brow (within him alone can spiritual blossoming arise, he alone can enjoy spiritual bliss). ||21||
Says Nanak, listen, O Saints: such a Sikh turns toward the Guru with sincere faith, and becomes sunmukh. ||21||
Says Nanak, hear, O saints, such a disciple turns towards the Guru.
Sri Guru Ji says: Listen, O sants! That Sikh becomes sanmukh before the Gurus. ||21||
18BG: Vemukhu = one who has turned his face the other way. Mukati = release from vices, release from the sway of Maya.

(Where there is dread on account of attachment to Maya, spiritual bliss cannot flourish; but) if any man turns his face away from the Guru (spiritual bliss cannot be his, because) without the Guru release from the sway of Maya is not had.
One who turns away from the Guru, and becomes baymukh - without the True Guru, he shall not find liberation.
If anyone turns away from the Guru; then he obtains not salvation without the True Guru.
If any sakat should turn his face from the Gurus, then without the sharan of the Satigurus he will not obtain mukti.
1T4C: Horthai = from any other place. Bibeki = a man of discernment, one able to judge. Jae = jai, having gone.
By all means go and ask any of the discerning (and satisfy yourself; it is a settled thing that apart from the Guru) release from the bonds of Maya is not had from any other place at all.
He shall not find liberation anywhere else either; go and ask the wise ones about this.
He shall obtain not salvation any where else. Go and consult the men of discrimination.
No one obtains mukti from any other place. Let anyone go and ask the discerning ones — the sense being, they too say this very thing.
E534: (The man caught in the attachment to Maya) comes wandering through countless births; without the Guru's shelter release from this attachment is not had.
He shall wander through countless incarnations; without the True Guru, he shall not find liberation.
He shall wander in many existences and obtain not deliverance without the True Guru.
He will come wandering in countless wombs; without the Satigurus he will not obtain mukti.
HWVB: In the end release from the attachment to Maya is had only by falling at the Guru's feet, because the Guru recites the updesh (of the true path of life).
But liberation is attained, when one is attached to the feet of the True Guru, chanting the Word of the Shabad.
He shall ultimately acquire emancipation, attaching himself to the feet of the True Guru, when he shall recite to him the Lord's Name.
If he then falls at the Guru's feet and the Satiguru recites the updesh, then he will obtain mukti.
9V88: Nanak says, reflect and see — without the Guru freedom from the bondage of Maya is not had, (and without this release the attainment of spiritual bliss cannot come about). ||22||
Says Nanak, contemplate this and see, that without the True Guru, there is no liberation. ||22||
Says Nanak, reflect over this and see that without the True Guru, deliverance is attained not.
Sri Guru Ji says: reflect and see, without the Satigurus this being never obtains mukti at all. ||22||
5A6J: Sachi bani = the bani of the praise of Parmatma, the bani that joins one to the ever-abiding Prabhu.
O Sikhs beloved of the Satiguru! Come, sing (together) the bani that joins one to the ever-abiding Parmatma.
Come, O beloved Sikhs of the True Guru, and sing the True Word of His Bani.
Come you the beloved disciples of the True Guru and sing the True hymns of the Guru.
Come, O Sikhs! Beloved of the Satigurus, sing the True Bani.
EPV2: Sir = upon the head, most excellent of all.
Sing the bani of your own Guru; this bani is supreme above all other banis.
Sing the Guru's Bani, the supreme Word of Words.
Sing you the word of the Guru. which word is the most sublime of all the words.
Sing the bani of the Gurus indeed; but among the banis know this to be the (siri) foremost bani.
DDQQ: Nadari = the glance of mercy. Karamu = bounty.
This bani settles only in the hearts of those men upon whom is Parmatma's glance of mercy, upon whom is His bounty.
Those who are blessed by the Lord's Glance of Grace - their hearts are imbued with this Bani.
Gurbani enters the mind of those, on whom the Lord casts His merciful glance.
Those upon whom is the (karamu) glance of grace of (nadari) Parmeshvar, in their heart it comes to dwell.
UBZE: Hari rangi = in the love of Hari. Sarig pani = the Prabhu who bears the bow. Keri = of. Amrit = the Nam-water that gives spiritual bliss.
(O beloved Gursikhs!) Remember the Nam of Parmatma, stay for ever joined in the love of Parmatma; drink this Nam-water (that gives bliss and produces spiritual uplift).
Drink in this Ambrosial Nectar, and remain in the Lord's Love forever; meditate on the Lord, the Sustainer of the world.
Quaff you Nectar, ever abide in God's love and reflect on God, the Earth-Sustainer.
Drinking the amrit of the Nam, remain for ever in the bliss of Hari; and keep repeating (sarigpani) Sarang, the bearer of the bow — that is, Parmeshvar.
UCDS: Nanak says, (O Gursikhs!) sing for ever this bani of the praise of Parmatma (in this alone is spiritual bliss). ||23||
Says Nanak, sing this True Bani forever. ||23||
Says Nanak, ever hymn you, this true word of the Guru.
Sri Guru Ji says: this very True Bani which concerns Bhagvant — sing it always. ||23||
R5BM: Satiguru bina = contrary to the Guru's intent.
Bani contrary to the Guru's intent is such as makes one waver before the glitter (of Maya).
Without the True Guru, other songs are false.
Without the True Guru, all other word is false.

Satiguru bina, that is to say, without the True-Formed and (guru) worshipful-formed Parmesur. The sense: that bani in which Parmesar's birth and deeds, and likewise His Nam, are not present, that is kachi. Is it then a thing that brings one to a fallen state? Upon this, the proof is Krishna Ji's statement to Uddhav in the eleventh skandh.
D2XF: Kachi = of light alloy, that which lowers the mind, that which brings one down from high spiritual bliss.
Bani contrary to the Guru's intent casts a man's mind down from the seat of spiritual bliss.
The songs are false without the True Guru; all other songs are false.
Without the True Guru every other word is false. All other sermons are but false.
The bani is indeed kachi without the Satigurus; but if any other should mislead you, do not be misled — hold to this certainty alone, that this bani is kachi.(1)
EF4C: Kache = those men whose mind is weak, who can waver before the influence of Maya. Sunde kache = the minds of the hearers too waver.

It is a settled thing that the minds of those who listen to bani which runs contrary to the Guru's intent become weak; the minds of the hearers too are made to waver; and those who read it over and over and expound it likewise become weak of mind.
The speakers are false, and the listeners are false; those who speak and recite are false.
False are the utterers, false the hearers, false the reciters and false their authors.
The speakers of that bani are kache, and its hearers too are kache, and its discourse too, spoken by the mouth, is kachi indeed.
U8YD: Kahia = whatever they say with the mouth.
Even if those men utter the Hari-Nam with the tongue, still no deep acquaintance with what they utter comes about for them,
They may continually chant, 'Har, Har' with their tongues, but they do not know what they are saying.
With their tongue they ever utter the Lord God's Name, but they realise not in the least what they say.
With the tongue they do indeed daily utter Hari; but of their own utterance, which is the shabad Hari Hari, they know nothing — the sense being, they do not take it into themselves.
E49U: Hiri laia = has stolen away. Ravani = merely with the tongue, only on the surface.
because Maya has kept their mind beguiled; whatever they utter, they utter only with the tongue.
Their consciousness is lured by Maya; they are just reciting mechanically.
They, whose mind is lured by mammon, continue reciting fluently and mechanically.
Those whose chit Maya has stolen away, they go on speaking (ravani) after the manner of the wind — that is, to no purpose; or, (ravani) they speak according to established custom.
T3PH: Kachi = by the kache, by those weak of mind ||24||
Nanak says, bani contrary to the Guru's intent casts a man's mind down from the seat of spiritual bliss. ||24||
Says Nanak, without the True Guru, other songs are false. ||24||
Says Nanak, without the True Guru all other gospel is false.
Sri Guru Ji says: without the Satigurus all other bani is kachi indeed. ||24||
UJ4T: Ratannu = ratan, priceless gift. Jitu = in which (shabad). Hire = the virtues of Parmatma. Jarau = set, inlaid.
The Satiguru's shabad is such a priceless gift that the greatnesses of Parmatma lie packed within it.
The Word of the Guru's Shabad is a jewel, studded with diamonds.
Guru's word is a jewel, which is studded with emeralds.
The updesh of the Gurus is (ratannu) priceless, in which the jewels of gian and the rest are set — the sense being, all the means are in the updesh itself.
0S9X: Mannu = mind. Ehu samau = such absorption.
The shabad is, as it were, such a jewel that by means of it a man's mind becomes settled (in the remembrance of Parmatma) and a wondrous absorption (in Parmatma) remains.
The mind which is attached to this jewel, merges into the Shabad.
He, whose mind is attached to this jewel of Gurbani, merges in it.
When the mind has become attached to the priceless updesh, then (ihu) this being's merging into Parmeshvar has come about.
YXC6: Sachai = in the ever-abiding Prabhu. Bhau = love.
If a man's mind becomes joined to the shabad, then (by virtue of this) his love for the ever-abiding Prabhu comes about.
One whose mind is attuned to the Shabad, enshrines love for the True Lord.
When man's mind is attuned to the word, he comes to enshrine affection for the True Lord.
He whose mind has met with the Guru's updesh, he has fixed his love upon (sachai) Vahiguru.
1C5U: (Within him the) diamond-Nam of Parmatma alone stays settled, the jewel-shabad (of Parmatma's praise) alone stays settled. (But this gift is had only by him) to whom (Prabhu Himself) grants this understanding.
He Himself is the diamond, and He Himself is the jewel; one who is blessed, understands its value.
The Lord Himself is the jewel and Himself the emerald. To whomsoever He blesses with Gurbani, to him He explains its worth.
That shabad of the Guru is itself the (hira) gian and itself the (ratanu) vairag; but he to whom Vahiguru gives the understanding, he knows it.
99QJ: Hira = the Nam of Parmatma. Ape = He Himself ||25||
Nanak says, the Guru's shabad is, as it were, a jewel in which the diamond that is Prabhu's Nam is set. ||25||
Says Nanak, the Shabad is a jewel, studded with diamonds. ||25||
Says Nanak, Guru's words is a jewel, which is enchased with emerald.
Sri Guru Ji says: the Guru's updesh is of the form of vairag, and with it the gian in the form of a diamond is inlaid. ||25||
QW7A: Siv = the conscious principle, the jivatma. Sakati = Maya. Ape = He Himself.
Having produced the jivatma and Maya, Parmatma Himself sets going (this) hukam, that (the force of Maya should bear upon the beings).
He Himself created Shiva and Shakti, mind and matter; the Creator subjects them to His Command.
Himself creating mind and matter, the Creator subjects them to His command.
(Siv) Ishar Himself, who is the Creator, having produced (sakati) — through Maya, the being, that is to say, by way of otherness — Himself also sets His hukam going over them.
BW7T: Hukamu = (this) hukam (that the influence of Maya should bear upon the beings). Gurmukhi = by way of the Guru. Kisai = to some (rare) one. Bujhae = He gives understanding.
Prabhu Himself sets this hukam going and Himself watches this play (of how the beings dance in Maya's hands); to some rare one He gives the understanding (of this play) by way of the Guru.
Enforcing His Order, He Himself sees all. How rare are those who, as Gurmukh, come to know Him.
The Lord enforces His order, He Himself sees all, Through the Guru, He makes some rare one know Him.
He sets the hukam going, He Himself watches the deeds of the being; but this understanding He explains to some gurmukh. The sense being, that Ishar is the giver of the fruit of the being's deeds.
79EN: Mukatu = free of the influence of Maya, independent. Manni = in the mind.
(In him to whom He grants understanding) He breaks the bonds of Maya, and that man becomes free of Maya's bonds, (because) he settles the Guru's shabad within his own mind.
They break their bonds, and attain liberation; they enshrine the Shabad within their minds.
He bursts his bonds, obtains emancipation and enshrines the Lord's Name in his mind.
This being then breaks the bonds and becomes mukat, when he settles the Guru's updesh in the mind.
ZFQX: Gurmukhi = one who walks upon the Guru's road.

Only that man is able to walk the road the Guru showed to whom Prabhu gives this capacity; that man joins his consciousness to the feet of the one Parmatma (within him spiritual bliss comes about, and he comes out of the attachment to Maya).
Those whom the Lord Himself makes Gurmukh, lovingly focus their consciousness on the One Lord.
He, whom the Lord Himself makes holy, becomes so and fixes his attention on the One Lord.
He whom Vahiguru Himself makes a gurmukh, he becomes one — he who joins his liv with the One.
CA75: Nanak says, Parmatma Himself makes (the jivatma and Maya) and Himself grants (to some rare one) the understanding (that the influence of Maya too is His own) hukam (at work in the world). ||26||
Says Nanak, He Himself is the Creator; He Himself reveals the Hukam of His Command. ||26||
Says Nanak, God Himself is the Creator and Himself reveals His will.
Sri Guru Ji says: that Creator Himself explains His own hukam. ||26||
D53B: The pandits who read the Simritis, Shastras and the rest reflect only upon this — what, according to these books, is sin and what is merit; the relish of spiritual bliss cannot come to them.
The Simritees and the Shaastras discriminate between good and evil, but they do not know the true essence of reality.
The Simritis and Shastras discriminate between good and evil, but know not the essence of the Real Thing.
The twenty-seven Simritis and the six Shastras reflect upon sin and merit and likewise upon their fruits; but through them the (sar) true account of the tat-sarup is not known.
9SCB: Tatai sar = the understanding of the essence, the understanding of reality, the understanding of what is truly worth grasping, the understanding of spiritual bliss.
(Know this for certain, that) without coming into the Satiguru's shelter the relish of spiritual bliss cannot come.
They do not know the true essence of reality without the Guru; they do not know the true essence of reality.
Without the Guru, they know not the essence of the Reality, know not the essence of the Reality.
Because without the Gurus, by the mere reflecting of those Shastras the essence of the sar was not known before; and even now the sar of the tat-sarup has been known by no one without the Guru.
XSZ9: Tihi guni = in the three dispositions of Maya. Bhrami = wandering and wandering. Raini = life, night.

The world lies heedless, wandering and wandering within the three gunas; the whole life passes in the sleep of attachment to Maya (the reflections of the Simritis and Shastras cannot wake one from this sleep).
The world is asleep in the three modes and doubt; it passes the night of its life sleeping.
The world is asleep in three modes and doubt, and in slumber its night(life) passes away.
Because the world sleeps in the delusion of the three gunas — that is, it has become ignorant; and through this alone the world's lifetime has passed away in sleep.
8K5G: Se = those men. Mani = in the mind.
(Out of the sleep of attachment) by the Guru's grace those men alone wake within whom the Nam of Parmatma dwells, who utter the bani of Parmatma's praise.
Those humble beings remain awake and aware, within whose minds, by Guru's Grace, the Lord abides; they chant the Ambrosial Word of the Guru's Bani.
By Guru's grace, only those mortals keep awake, in whose mind the Lord abides and who utter the Nectar-word.
By the Guru's mercy those persons have woken in whose mind Hari has come to dwell, and who with the mouth also utter the amrit of the Nam by way of bani.
GGQ6: Anadinu = every day, at every moment. Amrit bani = the bani that gives spiritual life. Jagat = staying alert against the vices ||27||
Nanak says, that man alone enjoys spiritual bliss who stays settled at every moment in the longing of Prabhu's remembrance, and whose life passes (thus, awake out of the sleep of attachment). ||27||
Says Nanak, they alone obtain the essence of reality, who night and day remain lovingly absorbed in the Lord; they pass the night of their life awake and aware. ||27||
Says Nanak, he alone obtains quintessence, who ever remains merged in the Lord's love and passes his life-night awake.
Sri Guru Ji says: he obtains the tat-sarup whose attention is fixed on Hari night and day, and whose lifetime has passed in (jagat) knowledge. ||27||
5PUH: Udar = belly. Manahu = from the mind. Kiu visariai = ought not to be forgotten.
(If spiritual bliss is to be obtained then) that Parmatma should never be forgotten who sustains us (even) within the mother's womb.
He nourished us in the mother's womb; why forget Him from the mind?
In our mind, why should we forget Him, who cherishes us in the mother's womb?
He who sustains within the mother's womb — why should such a capable One be forgotten from the mind?
RF9L: Evadu = so great. Agani = fire. Aharu = food.
So great a Giver ought not to be forgotten from the mind, who conveys food (even) into the fire (of the mother's womb).
Why forget from the mind such a Great Giver, who gave us sustenance in the fire of the womb?
Why should we forsake from our mind such a great Beneficent Lord, who reaches us sustenance in the midst of fire?
Why should so great a Giver be forgotten from the mind, who conveys food into the jatharagni?
L1Q2: Os no = to that man. Kihu = anything.
(It is attachment that keeps one deprived of bliss, but) nothing at all (of attachment and the rest) can touch that man to whom Prabhu grants the love of His own feet.
Nothing can harm one, whom the Lord inspires to embrace His Love.
Nothing can harm him whom the Lord blesses with His love.
That man to whom He attaches His own love — nothing can (pohi) afflict that man; the sense being, no obstacle befalls him.
